JUSTICE R.NATARAJ) M.F.A.Nos.202315 and 202316 of 2019 are filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Kalaburagi (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal) in M.V.C.No.983 and 984 of 2016, vide judgment and award dated 03.09.2018.

sentences.text: M.F.A.Nos.200093/2019 and 200094/2019 are filed by the insurer challenging its liability to pay the compensation in the aforesaid case.

2. The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- and Rs.15,00,000/- respectively for the injuries suffered by them in a road traffic incident on 26.04.2016, when the motorcycle on which they were riding were dashed against by a car bearing Reg.No.KA- 32/N-4074.
As a result of the accident, the claimants NC: 2026:KHC-K:1044-DB HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER suffered serious injuries and were treated at a hospital.

The claimants claimed that both of them were agricultural labourers and were earning Rs.20,000/- and Rs.15,000/- per month respectively and as a result of the injuries suffered, they were deprived of the income.

Therefore they claimed compensation from the owner and insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-32/N-4074.
3.

The insurer contested the claim petitions and claimed that the accident occurred on a highway and the claimants were rash and negligent in riding the motorcycle without exercising due care and caution while they entered the highway from a side road.

Therefore, it was contended that the The Divisional Manager, National ... vs Sangappa S/O Shantappa Biradar And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20637781/

It was also contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid licence as on the date of the accident.
Based on these contentions, the claim petitions were taken up for trial.

The claimants were examined and documents were marked on their behalf.
The insurer examined one of its official as RW-1, but did not mark any documents in evidence.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.

It held that the claimants had suffered injuries and based on the evidence of the doctor, it held that claimants had suffered disability to the extent of 7% to the whole body and considered their income at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month and awarded the following compensation:-

5. Since the offending vehicle was covered by a policy of insurance, the Tribunal directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded as well as the liability imposed on the insurer, both of them have filed these appeals.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal committed an error in construing the notional income of the claimants at a sum of Rs.7,500/-, while this Court has fixed a sum of - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1044-DB HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER Rs.8,750/- as the notional income for settlement before the Lok Adalat.
He therefore contends that the compensation determined by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer contended that the claimants had admitted in their evidence that they were travelling on their motorcycle on a side road and were about to enter the national highway, the accident happened.
She submits that therefore, they were bound to exercise due care and caution.
Contrarily, the claimants did not exercise due diligence but rammed against a car moving on the highway.
She therefore contends that the claimants had contributed to the accident and hence the insurer alone was not liable to pay the compensation.

She thus contends that the impugned judgment and award insofar as it fastens the liability to pay the entire compensation on the insurer be modified and the contributory negligence be suitably determined.

sentences.text: We have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.

9. As rightly contended by learned counsel for the claimants, this Court has considered notional income of a sum of Rs.8,750/- for settlement of claims arising out of accident that happen in the year 2016 before the Lok- adalat.
Therefore, there is no reason why the claimants should not be granted this benefit.
The Tribunal has considered the disability suffered by the claimants to the whole body at 7%.

Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimants and also having regard to the evidence adduced by the doctor before the Tribunal, we consider it appropriate to maintain the disability assessed by the Tribunal.

If we grant the benefit of a higher notional income of Rs.8,750/-,
then the compensation payable to the claimants would be as follows:

10 . As regards the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation, it may be that the claimants were moving from the side road to the main road.

However, that does not mean to say that the claimants were negligent and there is no evidence to establish that it is the claimants - 14 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1044-DB HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER who went and dashed against the car.

It appears that the car was moving on the highway at a high speed and the claimants were also moving towards the highway from a side road and without there being any conclusive evidence that the claimants were responsible for the accident, this Court is of the opinion that the claimants cannot be held negligent and cannot be held that they were responsible for causing the accident.
11. In that view of the matter, we do not propose to disturb the finding of the Tribunal insofar as liability of the insurer to pay the compensation.

Hence, the following order :
i) M.F.A.Nos.202315 and 202316 of 2019 filed by the claimants are allowed in part.
ii) The compensation determined by the Tribunal in MVC No.983/2016 is modified and enhanced from Rs.4,07,600/- to Rs.4,30,250/-, and in MVC No.984/2016 is modified and enhanced from Rs.2,48,600/- to Rs.2,66,000/- which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per The Divisional Manager, National ... vs Sangappa S/O Shantappa Biradar And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20637781/
10 - 15 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1044-DB HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

iii) The insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount within a period of one month from today, failing which, the insurer shall pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum and recover the excess interest payable from the person responsible for the delay in depositing the amount.
iv) M.F.A.Nos.200093/2019 and 200094/2019 filed by the insurer are dismissed.
v) Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.

The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- and Rs.15,00,000/- respectively for the injuries suffered by them in a road traffic incident on 26.04.2016, when the motorcycle on which they were riding were dashed against by a car bearing Reg.No.KA- 32/N-4074.
As a result of the accident, the claimants NC: 2026:KHC-K:1044-DB HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER suffered serious injuries and were treated at a hospital.
The claimants claimed that both of them were agricultural labourers and were earning Rs.20,000/- and Rs.15,000/- per month respectively and as a result of the injuries suffered, they were deprived of the income.
Therefore they claimed compensation from the owner and insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-32/N-4074.
3.
The insurer contested the claim petitions and claimed that the accident occurred on a highway and the claimants were rash and negligent in riding the motorcycle without exercising due care and caution while they entered the highway from a side road.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
It held that the claimants had suffered injuries and based on the evidence of the doctor, it held that claimants had suffered disability to the extent of 7% to the whole body and considered their income at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month and awarded the following compensation:-
5. Since the offending vehicle was covered by a policy of insurance, the Tribunal directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded as well as the liability imposed on the insurer, both of them have filed these appeals.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
She thus contends that the impugned judgment and award insofar as it fastens the liability to pay the entire compensation on the insurer be modified and the contributory negligence be suitably determined.
9. As rightly contended by learned counsel for the claimants, this Court has considered notional income of a sum of Rs.8,750/- for settlement of claims arising out of accident that happen in the year 2016 before the Lok- adalat.
Therefore, there is no reason why the claimants should not be granted this benefit.
The Tribunal has considered the disability suffered by the claimants to the whole body at 7%.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimants and also having regard to the evidence adduced by the doctor before the Tribunal, we consider it appropriate to maintain the disability assessed by the Tribunal.
However, that does not mean to say that the claimants were negligent and there is no evidence to establish that it is the claimants - 14 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1044-DB HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER who went and dashed against the car.
It appears that the car was moving on the highway at a high speed and the claimants were also moving towards the highway from a side road and without there being any conclusive evidence that the claimants were responsible for the accident, this Court is of the opinion that the claimants cannot be held negligent and cannot be held that they were responsible for causing the accident.
